identification.summary: Mustard Tempest is Microsoft's name for the activity group behind the FakeUpdates (SocGholish) JavaScript backdoor and its fake-browser-update delivery; Microsoft originally tracked it as DEV-0206 and announced the rename in an April 2023 update [S1]. MITRE describes the group as an initial access broker that has operated the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017 and has partnered with Indrik Spider to deliver additional malware [S10]. Proofpoint tracks the same SocGholish activity as TA569 and Mandiant tracks the FakeUpdates chain as UNC1543 [S3][S5].
identification.firstObserved: 2017 (MITRE: operating the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017) [S10]
identification.notes: Aliases in the record: DEV-0206 (Microsoft), INDRIK SPIDER (listed against this actor in the record's Microsoft mapping source; CrowdStrike name for the Evil Corp-associated cluster, so treat as an overlap not an identity) [S11]. TA569 (Proofpoint) [S3]. UNC1543 (Mandiant) [S5]. GOLD PRELUDE (Secureworks) appears in secondary reporting only [S8]. Boundary: Microsoft tracks Evil Corp-overlapping ransomware activity separately as DEV-0243, and Mandiant tracks the Evil Corp-overlapping cluster as UNC2165; these are customers or partners of the access operation, not the same cluster [S1][S5]. Microsoft's October 2022 report did not itself describe DEV-0206 as an initial access broker; that characterisation comes from MITRE and Proofpoint [S1][S3][S10].

attribution.basis: No state sponsor is asserted in the cited sources. Proofpoint describes TA569 as a financially motivated cybercriminal actor and an initial access broker [S3]. Microsoft places the actor in its financially motivated Tempest family [S1][S11]. The country field in the record (FIN) is not supported by any cited source and should be treated as unverified. The 2026 Operation Endgame action was reported by secondary outlets as a law enforcement operation involving Dutch police, RCMP, FBI, BKA, Europol and Eurojust against infrastructure tied to TA569 [S8]; no indictment or named individuals were found in the sources reviewed.

objectives: Financial gain through selling or handing off footholds on compromised enterprise hosts to ransomware and malware operators (initial access brokerage / pay-per-install) [S3][S10]. Microsoft observed FakeUpdates activity leading to follow-on hands-on activity resembling DEV-0243 (Evil Corp-overlapping) pre-ransomware behaviour [S1][S4].

sectors: Opportunistic across sectors (victims arrive via compromised websites)
Government (reported as among most affected in early 2025 SocGholish detections, per secondary reporting of Trend Micro)
Healthcare (reported RansomHub follow-on, per secondary reporting)
regions: United States (highest detections early 2025, per secondary reporting)
targeting.notes: Targeting is driven by which websites are compromised and who visits them rather than by victim selection; the 2026 takedown reporting describes 14,971 compromised WordPress sites cleaned [S8][S9]. The sector and region claims above come from search-result summaries of Trend Micro and Trustwave reporting that could not be opened; treat as unverified (see gaps).

capabilities.summary: FakeUpdates (SocGholish) is a JavaScript backdoor delivered primarily through drive-by downloads or malicious ads posing as browser updates [S1]. Secondary reporting describes compromised legitimate websites that present fake Chrome or Firefox update prompts and chain through a traffic distribution system; site compromise reportedly occurs via vulnerable CMS plugins or themes and weak or reused credentials [S7][S8]. Microsoft observed the same backdoor delivered onto Raspberry Robin-infected devices beginning 26 July 2022 [S1]. Follow-on tooling attributed to partner clusters includes Cobalt Strike loaders, WastedLocker and later LockBit and RansomHub payloads, delivered by other actors after access is handed off [S2][S4][S5][S10].

attack.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

campaigns.name: SocGholish distribution network operating
campaigns.summary: MITRE states the group has operated the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017 [S10].

campaigns.name: Partnership with Evil Corp-overlapping actor for WastedLocker
campaigns.summary: Per press coverage of Microsoft's reporting, DEV-0243's initial partnerships with DEV-0206 involved deploying the WastedLocker ransomware payload, before DEV-0243 expanded to other in-house payloads [S4]. MITRE likewise states the group partnered with Indrik Spider to deliver WastedLocker, LockBit and remote access tools [S10].

campaigns.name: Mandiant links FakeUpdates chain (UNC1543) to UNC2165 and LockBit
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reported that UNC2165, overlapping with Evil Corp, relied almost entirely on the FakeUpdates chain that Mandiant tracks as UNC1543, and had shifted to LockBit ransomware, which Mandiant assessed as a way to obscure the affiliation and sanctions exposure (secondary reporting) [S5].

campaigns.name: FakeUpdates delivered via Raspberry Robin
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed the first reported instance of a Raspberry Robin-infected host receiving FakeUpdates on 26 July 2022, which led to DEV-0243 activity. Microsoft tracks the Raspberry Robin operators separately as DEV-0856 [S1].

campaigns.name: News-site compromise campaign
campaigns.summary: TechCrunch reported on a crime group hijacking hundreds of US news websites to push malware, with Proofpoint's view that TA569 brokers access to Evil Corp but is not Evil Corp (title and snippet only; article not opened) [S6].

campaigns.name: Microsoft renames DEV-0206 to Mustard Tempest
campaigns.summary: Microsoft updated its report to state DEV-0206 is now tracked as Mustard Tempest [S1].

campaigns.name: RansomHub deployed after Mustard Tempest access
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence stated RansomHub was observed deployed in post-compromise activity by Manatee Tempest following initial access by Mustard Tempest via FakeUpdates/SocGholish infections [S2].

campaigns.name: Silent Push infrastructure analysis
campaigns.summary: Silent Push research on SocGholish infrastructure was reported as showing the malware spread via ad tools and delivering access to LockBit, Evil Corp and others (headline-level only; body not opened) [S7].

campaigns.name: Operation Endgame action against SocGholish infrastructure
campaigns.summary: Secondary reporting states Dutch police and prosecutors with RCMP, FBI, BKA, Europol and Eurojust took down 106 servers and domains and cleaned 14,971 compromised WordPress sites tied to TA569/SocGholish. Domain counts vary between outlets and the primary law enforcement releases were not reviewed [S8][S9].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated initial access broker tracked as DEV-0206 / Mustard Tempest (Microsoft), TA569 (Proofpoint), UNC1543 (Mandiant); partner relationships with Evil Corp-overlapping clusters (DEV-0243, UNC2165) [S1][S3][S5][S10].
diamond.capability: FakeUpdates/SocGholish JavaScript backdoor and fake browser update lures; hand-off of access to partners who use Cobalt Strike and ransomware [S1][S10].
diamond.infrastructure: Network of compromised legitimate websites (reported as WordPress and other CMS) redirecting through a traffic distribution system to fake update pages; 106 servers and domains reported seized in June 2026 [S7][S8].
diamond.victim: Enterprise users visiting compromised sites; victims in the US and government and healthcare organisations reported in secondary sources [S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Cybercriminal ecosystem relationship with Evil Corp-overlapping actors, which are subject to Western sanctions per Mandiant's reporting; no state tasking is cited [S5].
diamond.technology: Browsers and web servers/CMS on the website side; Windows endpoints executing downloaded JavaScript; Microsoft lists Defender detections such as Trojan:JS/Socgolsh.A and Trojan:JS/FakeUpdate.B [S1].

gaps: Proofpoint, Mandiant, Secureworks and Trend Micro primary reports could not be opened (hosts blocked from this environment); vendor statements are taken from search-result summaries and secondary outlets.
Proofpoint's high-confidence WastedLocker association and its statement that TA569 is not Evil Corp were seen only in search summaries; publication dates for those posts were not verified.
Secureworks GOLD PRELUDE primary reporting not found; one third-party post treats GOLD PRELUDE as a separate downstream actor, which conflicts with other sources.
Country/origin (FIN in the record) is unsupported by cited sources.
Primary Europol, FBI and Dutch police releases for the June 2026 action were not reviewed; counts of domains and credentials differ across outlets.
Sector and region statistics (US, government, healthcare) come from secondary summaries of Trend Micro and Trustwave and are unverified.
Relationship between this cluster and Raspberry Robin (DEV-0856) operators, and the exact commercial terms with Evil Corp, are not established in the sources.
Microsoft's report did not describe DEV-0206 as an access broker nor link it to Cobalt Strike; the MITRE ATT&CK Cobalt Strike association is partner-attributed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2 (battlespace): the relevant terrain is the commercial web, where compromised legitimate sites are the delivery layer, and enterprise endpoints that browse the internet [S1][S7]. Step 3 (adversary): a financially motivated access broker feeding Evil Corp-overlapping and RaaS operators; its output is access, so downstream effects are ransomware and hands-on intrusions [S2][S4][S5][S10]. Step 4 MLCOA (assessed): continued fake-update lures from newly compromised sites, with access passed to ransomware affiliates, possibly slowed by the June 2026 takedown [S8]. MDCOA (assessed): re-establishment on new infrastructure and use against high-value networks, including defense-related staff browsing from enterprise endpoints. Candidate indicators: browser-update prompts from non-vendor domains, wscript/JavaScript execution from downloads, Defender detections named Socgolsh or FakeUpdate [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: monitor for FakeUpdates/Socgolsh detections and for follow-on Cobalt Strike activity after web-borne infections [S1][S10]. Authorities: the actor is criminal, so response lies mainly in defensive cyberspace operations and law enforcement coordination rather than military action. Mission assurance: enforce script-execution restrictions, block user-run downloads from browsers, and apply Microsoft's published mitigations (tamper protection, cloud-delivered protection, attack surface reduction rules) [S1]. Coordination: share indicators with the DoD Cyber Crime Center and commercial partners, and watch for follow-on ransomware affiliates because access is resold [S2][S4].

provenance.importedSummary: Mustard Tempest is an initial access broker that has operated the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017. Mustard Tempest has partnered with Indrik Spider to provide access for the download of additional malware including LockBit, WastedLocker, and remote access tools.
